promises.text: The Long road from Archon to Gideon crosses Middle Argonia on what firm ground it can find. Here that is a strip of ground between two meres, barely higher than the water.

confirmed.note: The road runs on a mud strip 15-25 m wide between the mere and the marsh pond; the layout stands on that strip.

promises.text: Nobody lives on the neck. Travellers drove poles into both verges so that a walker can keep to the causeway when the water covers it.

confirmed.note: No dwelling or bed on the neck; 22 driven poles stand on both verges of the wade, bound to the two wade-head parcels.

promises.text: The poles rot in the mud and lean. A walker who strays off the causeway between them goes into deeper water.

confirmed.note: The poles stand on both verges of the wade at their own yaws; off the causeway the water is deeper than the 0.1-1.28 m on the road line.

promises.text: The neck is the only dry line between the meres for a long way. For about fifty metres the mere covers the north half of the road, knee-deep and in places to the waist.

confirmed.note: From x 4787 to 4736 the north verge poles stand in 0.26-0.83 m of water and the road line in 0.1-1.28 m (chunk ground); the south verge is dry; cairns mark both dry ends.

promises.text: If the meres dried back, the poles would be left standing on dry ground. Nobody would replace them.

confirmed.note: The poles stand in the water along the wade, where only the wet ground explains them.
